working: Polarity is judged on the usual solvent-polarity (eluotropic) scale, which reflects hydrogen bonding and overall solvent polarity rather than dipole moment alone. Diethyl ether has only a weakly polar C–O–C group and is the least polar. Acetone has a polar C=O group but cannot donate hydrogen bonds. Ethanol has an O–H group and forms hydrogen bonds. Acetic acid has a –COOH group with strong hydrogen bonding and is the most polar. So the order is A < C < B < D, which is option 4. Caveat: by gas-phase dipole moment alone, acetone (about 2.9 D) exceeds ethanol (about 1.7 D). The question presumably intends the solvent-polarity scale.
